verdict.rationale: Statsig documents programmatic flag management: the Console API is a CRUD API for console actions, and the Statsig CLI manages Feature Gates and can run in CI/CD pipelines. There is also an official MCP server, though its docs describe asking questions and exploring data rather than writing changes. Nothing in the evidence shows approval or review workflows that force agent-made flag changes through sign-off before reaching production; environment-tier isolation is a different control. Missing for 10: documented approval/review workflows gating flag changes, evidence that the MCP server can create or toggle flags, and hands-on corroboration of agent-driven flag writes.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can create and toggle flags through documented APIs, CLIs, or MCP — and the platform can force my changes through approval workflows instead of letting me write to production unreviewed

citations.quote: The Console API is the CRUD API for performing the actions available on console.statsig.com without using the web UI.
The Statsig CLI is a command-line interface that helps manage Feature Gates, Experiments, and Dynamic Configs within the Statsig platform.
You can integrate the CLI into CI/CD pipelines to automate the management of Feature Gates and Experiments.
